storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content: This projected body remains in the form of a girl who passed away prematurely. With tattered clothes, pale skin, and eyes filled with shadows of the past, it silently tells of a history entwined with illness and suffering.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
This is a souvenir Professor Dexter brought back from the Febvre Coast.

The mild ocean climate of Febvre is very pleasant. The century-old Sevada Sanatorium is located by the seashore, attracting countless vacationers each year.

In this glass bottle, wrapped in seaweed, are some translucent powders. It is neither a message left by shipwreck survivors nor a local sand art piece. Professor Dexter has noticed that the bottle contains silver essence powder, meaning it houses a spirit.

He said he bought it from a local fisherman who hesitantly narrated recent strange encounters. A few days ago, early in the morning, the fisherman encountered an unusual fish swarm while fishing. It was neither the breeding season nor the wintering season, yet the swarm lingered. When the heavy nets were pulled up, they found a strange bottle. The fisherman, curious but uneasy, feared the bottle might bring bad luck or a curse. After this, no fish were caught in this area for several days.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
She treats every person and every Awakener with great kindness, never showing any signs of aggression. Most of the time, she stays quietly in her room, gazing out the window. At her bedside, we discovered several well-worn classical novels, along with handwritten essays and poems on notepaper, written in a delicate, graceful hand.

"Compared to that Maiden, I am clearly the lucky one." She whispered to the shimmering campus pond, facing the setting sun.

She rarely takes part in outdoor activities—though rather than saying she is unwilling, it might be more accurate to say she simply doesn't know how. That Maiden-like Awakener seems to lack a great deal of common knowledge about everyday life.

On several occasions, we also witnessed her conversing with the fish in the fountain in a strange sound—like bubbles being exhaled, or the hoarse gurgle of someone drowning. Yet her expression remained calm and serene, as if she were exchanging comfort with a dear friend. In that moment, we all believed she had found true peace.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
One step, then another, I slowly walked into the water. The nurse at the sanatorium never allowed me to go this far. I hope a patient who will soon be unable to afford the sanatorium's fees doesn't cause her too much blame.

The sunset's afterglow reflected on the sea. Waves approached gently, lifting my skirt softly. The seawater's body temperature felt warm like a mother's embrace.

My body had never felt as light as it did at this moment; a desolate volcano lay within my chest, and now only the sea breeze remained there.

"Let's go home."

I heard the sea calling me in my parents' voices. They went to the other side of the sea to raise money for my treatment. If I hadn't been given such an unfortunate body, they wouldn't have had to struggle so much. If only I could vanish quietly into the sea on a moonlit night... I had thought this countless times, but thinking of my parents' sorrowful faces, I could only give up.

But one day, on a moonlit night, the ship my parents were on quietly disappeared into the sea.

"Let's go home."

I used all my strength to quicken my pace. The sea always calmly accepts all the suffering souls, and for me, the place where my parents are is the eternal refuge.

When the darkness descends from all sides, I was finally able to breathe freely for the first time in my life

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
I love the sea. Febvre's sea. The Prussian blue sea. The sea with warm, moist breezes. The sea that looks like a painting from the sanatorium's window. The sea with returning sails. The sea nurturing countless lives like a mother.

Now, I've finally returned to the tranquil sea, back to before birth, back to being enveloped in my mother's amniotic fluid. The currents gather the unfortunate Fragments, piecing me together among bones and coral. The deep-sea fish swim past, listening to the laments of fate's suffering.

Mother, if I could be born again, would I be happier?

daily.title: Awaken
daily.content: Greetings. I am Nymphaea of Febvre. You have granted me a new body, allowing me to finally breathe freely... How may I repay this grace?

daily.title: Upgrade: I
daily.content: I feel much better now, thank you for your kindness.

daily.title: Upgrade: II
daily.content: Do you think I might become stronger, too?

daily.title: Upgrade: III
daily.content: If it pleases you, I would like to present a pale purple water-lily as a token of my sincere gratitude.

daily.title: Enlighten: Observe
daily.content: I would be grateful for your effort.

daily.title: Enlighten: Ponder
daily.content: My body feels warm, as if gently enveloped by the sea. It is truly incredible.

daily.title: Enlighten: Reflect
daily.content: Can this feeling truly be called "happiness"? I... never dared to hope for it before.

daily.title: Enlighten: Insight
daily.content: To be saved by you, I often feel a happiness that terrifies me... Please tell me this is not a dream, and that you will not vanish into the sea without a trace, will you?

daily.title: Enlighten: Elevate
daily.content: The sea has its own language. Just like this... I can sometimes chat with the little fish in the pond about our hometown. If you are curious, I can help translate for you.

daily.title: Enlighten: Florish
daily.content: Next time, let us go see the sea together. Febvre is fine; I can be your guide. Or anywhere else, even to the ends of the earth—I want to go with you.

daily.title: Affinity: I
daily.content: During my time at the sanatorium, I tried making friends, but people were reluctant to approach me... Is it because of this bone-eroding "poison"? Please, be careful when you come near me.

daily.title: Affinity: II
daily.content: The sound of the bell carried by the night wind brings such peace. Would you like to sit on the stone chair and listen for a while? I will properly prepare your seat with a scarf.

daily.title: Affinity: III
daily.content: Have you heard of "sea burial"? In my old town, there was a custom of submerging the deceased into the sea; the ocean became everyone's final resting place. As for me, I returned to its embrace early...

daily.title: Affinity: IV
daily.content: Withering before blooming, like a water-lily... Seeking peace in the cold, raging tides, too timid to pursue my own happiness... That is the kind of person I am, Keeper.

daily.title: Affinity: V
daily.content: I once grappled with this dilemma: Is pain longer than life itself? If so, is a peaceful slumber happier than tormented wakefulness? After waking, I too was ensnared, until you brought me this safe haven...

daily.title: Chat: Touch
daily.content: Let's slow down a bit... Is there anything at all I can do for you?

daily.title: Chat: About Reading
daily.content:
<Italic:"The ruffled water-lilies are sighing around her;
At times she rouses, in a slumbering alder,
Some nest from which escapes a small rustle of wings;
A mysterious anthem falls from the golden stars.">
Ah, sorry—have I been reciting too loudly? It is one of my favorite poems... Would you like to read it with me?

daily.title: Chat: About Murphy
daily.content: Though our temperaments differ, I truly admire that child. She possesses a courage that transcends all hardships and limitations. If I had been as brave and resilient as her, perhaps I would not have chosen to end my life in the sea...

daily.title: Chat: About Celeste
daily.content: I deeply admire her—the maritime goddess, as pure and elegant as a lily... You say even she could not control her fate and ultimately sank into the sea? It is truly hard to imagine...

daily.title: Chat: About Dissolution
daily.content: After coming to school, I finally understood the disease called Dissolution that infected me. My parents always kept me away from the ocean when I was alive, and now it seems this infection might indeed be connected to my proximity to the sea...

daily.title: Chat: About Mythag
daily.content: Compared to others, Nymphaea is simply an ordinary person with no achievements or value. Why have I become an Awakener... it must be some small, humble wish.

daily.title: Chat: What I Like
daily.content: Do you like the sea? I love the sea no matter what. I still remember that day many years ago when the sea gently delivered long-awaited death to the unfortunate me.

daily.title: Chat: What I Hate
daily.content: Hate? I hate an inescapable fate and an inevitable tragedy.

daily.title: Chat: About the Keeper
daily.content: Thank you for your kindness in providing me shelter. I hope I won't bring a tragic fate upon you...

battle.title: Investigation Begins
battle.content: I will properly complete the task you have assigned to me.

battle.title: Investigation Success
battle.content: Did it... truly work? Have I been of any genuine help?

battle.title: Investigation Halted
battle.content: Do not lose heart. The sea embraces us all.

battle.title: Skill: II
battle.content: Do you hear me? Do you truly hear my voice?

battle.title: Rouse
battle.content: Now, it is my turn to repay you.

battle.title: Exalt
battle.content: May the deep sea grant you eternal rest.

battle.title: Over-Exalt
battle.content: <Italic:"...Oui tu mourus, enfant, par un fleuve emportée!">
